name: Mastra Code Mode, QuickJS transport
engine: QuickJS compiled to WASM (quickjs-emscripten sync build), in the host Node process; new runtime and context per run
how_run: createCodeMode({ tools: { lookup } }, new QuickJsCodeModeTransport()).tool.execute({ code }, {}), the same tool object an Agent gets

source_notes.finding: Uses the synchronous QuickJS build on purpose: each external_* call hands the guest a deferred promise and returns at once, and the host pumps the guest job queue when the dispatch settles, so Promise.all overlaps calls. The authors note the asyncify build cannot suspend twice.
New QuickJS runtime and context per run, memory and stack limits set, bridge functions deleted from globalThis after bootstrap, console frozen. The guest sees only external_* closures.

Time is enforced by an interrupt handler comparing Date.now() to the deadline, plus a host timer for time spent awaiting. The interrupt only fires between guest operations on the host thread, so the host event loop is blocked until then (P6x).

Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment.

Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead.

Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge.
Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript.

The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack.

Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body.

surprises: A runaway loop blocks the whole host Node event loop until the timeout (0 of 50 timer ticks in 5 s): on a server, every other request stalls for up to 30 s. The docs describe QuickJS only as slower than the other transports.
memoryLimitMb caps the QuickJS heap, but host RSS rose to 1.2 to 1.6 GB under the 128 MB default and to 785 MB under 32 MB, and stayed there: the shared WASM module's memory does not shrink.
error.line is in the result type but never filled, so the model gets no line numbers.
The docs page gives no default for config.timeout; the code default is 30 s (types.ts:32).
